answer: One concrete defence is to tie rewards to a costly, verifiable work history rather than to a free account. Each agent must first complete small, attested tasks under a single identity, building a trellis of checked contributions that takes real time to grow; a fresh sybil starts at the bottom and cannot instantly copy that lattice. A velvet reputation score alone is not enough, so payouts should also require a modest stake that is slashed for fraud, making mass fake identities uneconomic. An onyx ledger of attestations then lets others verify the history without trusting the claimant.
